A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RelaxFlow. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component and sensitivity ablations, qualitative experiments, and a 32-participant user study in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, a 100-case evaluation, and runtime and memory measurements in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The dual-branch procedure, multi-prior conditioning, attention-logit smoothing, temporal schedule, and visibility-aware fusion remain unchanged. The new direct text+image fusion procedure is a comparison baseline, not a modification of RelaxFlow.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same data sources and task types, including extreme occlusion, semantic branching, and conflicting-condition examples. The new 100-case AmbiSem-3D-Ext split uses ObjaverseXL and emphasizes view-induced ambiguity, which v1 already explicitly includes. It expands sampling within existing coverage rather than establishing a distinct domain or task.

E2.justification: New Tables 3–4 evaluate four additional comparator families on both benchmarks: Wan2.2-TI2V + TRELLIS, MV-Adapter + TRELLIS, TRELLIS text+image fusion, and Nano Banana Pro + 3D. Original comparators remain; the change from '2D Edit' to 'SDXL' in Table 2 identifies the existing baseline more explicitly.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate 100-case evaluation selected through multi-view caption disagreement and manual filtering, plus runtime/memory testing on a 10-sample random subset using an RTX A5000. Additional comparison protocols introduce video/multi-view generation followed by reconstruction and direct text-image fusion. Original benchmark settings, metrics, defaults, and user-study design are retained.

E4.justification: The original component, hyperparameter, prior-count, and prior-source ablations and RelaxFlow conflict cases remain unchanged. Figures 9–11 add diagnostic case studies of alternative pipelines' branch misalignment, reconstruction inconsistency, and attribute leakage; Table 6 adds computational-cost analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The new 100-case evaluation and 10-sample timing subset concern evaluation sample sizes, not repeated runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–2 and ablation values are unchanged, but Tables 3–6 add substantial results. On the extension, RelaxFlow scores 0.845/26.9 versus SAM3D's 0.839/25.6 for CLIP image/text alignment. Newly evaluated Nano Banana Pro exceeds RelaxFlow in text alignment on both original benchmarks. Runtime measurements report 2.46× and 1.82× backbone costs for SAM3D and TRELLIS respectively.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same mathematical definitions, spectral assumptions, stability analysis, and Wasserstein bounds and proofs. Typographical corrections and an optimal-transport citation update do not change the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same task formulation, training-free framework, theoretical justification, and two diagnostic benchmarks. Additional evaluations do not redefine these principal claims.

C2.justification: v1's claim of negligible computational overhead is replaced by acknowledgment of increased runtime and a memory/runtime tradeoff. Appendix E also explains the new baselines' failure mechanisms and describes text alignment as competitive rather than universally best. The original compatibility limitation and low-pass interpretation remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the extension's candidate-mining and filtering process, new baseline compositions, the Wan prompting template, and hardware and resource measurements for the cost study. Original implementation defaults, visibility-mask details, and repository access information are retained. Specific mining-model identities remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Wan, MV-Adapter, Nano Banana Pro, and additional completion, affordance, and visual-token research, while extending discussion of alternative conditioning routes. The central novelty argument remains unchanged. Interp3D and optimal-transport bibliographic updates refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. Changes include grammar fixes, a clearer Section 5.4 title, affiliation and publication-status updates, acknowledgements, an impact statement, and a new Appendix E with subsequent appendix renumbering.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 and the visual ablation are reformatted as larger, full-width displays. v2 adds dataset galleries in Figures 7–8, baseline visualizations in Figures 9–11, and Tables 3–6. Existing supplementary figures are retained and relocated, with extensive reflow of the surrounding layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility through four additional comparison families and evaluation beyond the original 21 manually curated ambiguity cases. It also corrects the unsupported negligible-overhead assertion with measured costs and exposes text-alignment tradeoffs. Missing uncertainty estimates and incomplete new configuration details remain limitations, but the broader validation and more accurate account of practical costs resolve important weaknesses in v1.
